name: Easlo
tagline: Notion templates for students and solo workers, sold on Gumroad
summary: Easlo is the brand of Jason Chin, who sells Notion templates such as the Second Brain system. He reported $239K revenue in 2022 as a one-person operation and said in March 2023 he was halfway to $1M in cumulative revenue.
origin: Chin taught himself Notion from YouTube while a student. In summer 2021 he released free templates (budget and habit trackers) on Gumroad with an optional tip and promoted them on Twitter and Product Hunt. After receiving tips of up to $100, he began charging for new templates in November 2021.
howItMakesMoney: One-time purchases of Notion templates on Gumroad. The flagship Second Brain template has been sold at $130 and reportedly passed $100K in sales on its own; smaller single-purpose templates sell for less.
growth: Released templates free with 'pay what you want' first, building a list of past downloaders before charging
Targeted a narrow starting niche (students organizing school, money and health)
Posted template screenshots and short threads on X, and later Instagram and TikTok
Bundled smaller templates into a premium all-in-one Second Brain product at a higher price
moat: Weak on the product (templates are easy to copy) but strong on distribution: a large social following and brand recognition in the Notion template niche.
risks: Depends on Notion's popularity and on Notion's own template marketplace; AI tools that generate workspaces could commoditize templates.

timeline.event: Releases free Notion templates on Gumroad with optional tips
Says he is halfway to $1M in total revenue

lessons: Launching free with an optional tip is a cheap way to test which product people value
Start with a niche you are part of (he was a student making student templates)
A bundle of existing pieces can be the highest-priced product
Visual products sell well on visual social platforms; screenshots are the ad

rebuild.idea: Operating templates for a specific regulated small business (e.g. solo physiotherapists or tutors) in Notion or Airtable, covering intake, scheduling and compliance records
rebuild.why: General productivity templates are saturated, but vertical templates that encode a profession's actual workflow are rare and buyers can expense them.
mvp: Interview 5 practitioners in one profession about their admin workflow
Build one template for their most painful workflow and give it to those 5 free
Publish a $49 version on Gumroad and post walkthrough videos in that profession's groups
Add a paid setup call as an upsell
rebuild.fit: Someone who works in or alongside that profession and knows Notion or Airtable well

sources.title: Business Insider (via Yahoo Finance): I made $239,000 this year selling templates
Ben Lang: tens of thousands of customers selling Notion templates, meet Easlo
